page: Amazon Web Services c8g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture, it features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 (ARMv9) model running at 2.8 GHz. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance. The server achieved top-tier status in Geekbench multi-core testing, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark database operations. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, scoring in the top tier for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read/write operations. In application-specific workloads, the instance demonstrated top-tier performance in static web serving throughput and medium-model LLM text generation. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark physics tests also registered in the top tier, while single-core performance and text processing benchmarks remained in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture and dedicated physical cores deliver high multi-threaded performance per resource unit, though the 2.0 GB per core memory ratio represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications. The lack of local storage requires external network-attached storage configurations. This server is optimized for highly parallelized workloads, including software compilation, database operations, static web serving, multi-threaded data decompression, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
